name: Cable Low Flye to Press
description: A combination movement that begins as a low-to-high cable flye targeting the upper pectoralis major, then transitions into a press motion at the top of the arc to fully extend the arms and further load the chest. This two-phase movement recruits both the isolation benefits of the flye and the loading capacity of the press in a single continuous rep.

execution.starting_position: Stand between two low cable pulleys. Hold one handle in each hand, cables running from low pulleys below hip level. Stand tall with a slight forward lean, arms extended down and to the sides.
execution.setup_instructions: Set both pulleys to the lowest position. Attach single D-handles. Stand centered between the two stacks.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arms extended downward and outward, cables taught from the low pulleys.
Step 2: Sweep both arms upward and inward in a wide arc — the flye phase — keeping elbows slightly bent.
Step 3: As the hands meet in front of the chest, transition to a press: bend the elbows and bring the handles toward the chest.
Step 4: Press the handles forward and together to full arm extension.
Step 5: Reverse the motion: unpress back to handle-at-chest, then open out and down in the flye return. Repeat.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale through the flye and press phases combined. Inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Transitioning to the press too early before the hands meet
Excessive forward lean that reduces the cable's tension angle effectiveness
Straightening elbows completely during the flye — maintain a soft bend
safety_considerations: Use moderate weight — the transition from flye to press can stress the shoulder if too heavy
Keep core braced throughout to stabilize the torso
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full sweep from low-to-high, then full press extension. The combo requires deliberate transition at the midpoint.
coaching_cues: Flye first, then press — two distinct phases per rep
Lead with the chest, not the arms, on the upward sweep
